bib.title: Is ChatGPT a General-Purpose Natural Language Processing Task Solver?
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 1339-1384

question: Is ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo) a general-purpose NLP task solver in the zero-shot setting, and on which task types does it do well or fall behind?
contributions: First study of ChatGPT's zero-shot capabilities on a diverse range of NLP tasks (20 datasets, 7 task categories)
Comparison with GPT-3.5 (text-davinci-003) and with zero-shot, few-shot and fine-tuned results reported in other work
Qualitative case studies and per-class analyses explaining where ChatGPT gains or loses

method.summary: Zero-shot prompting of gpt-3.5-turbo (ChatGPT) and text-davinci-003 (GPT-3.5) on 20 datasets across reasoning, NLI, QA, dialogue, summarization, NER and sentiment, with single-stage prompts and a Kojima-style two-stage zero-shot-CoT for reasoning. Results are compared with numbers reported in earlier papers for FLAN, T0, PaLM, fine-tuned models and others.
method.task: zero-shot evaluation of an instruction-tuned chat LLM across NLP task categories

models.name: ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo)
models.architecture: GPT-3.5 series model trained with RLHF

other.note: zero-shot and few-shot numbers in Tables 2-3 are from Wei et al. 2022 / Kojima et al. 2022

inference.samples: not stated; a single result per dataset is reported, no seeds, repeated runs or variance
inference.prompting: zero-shot, single-stage: task instruction P concatenated with test input X, Y = f(P, X). Zero-shot-CoT for reasoning tasks is two-stage as in Kojima et al. 2022: stage 1 uses 'Let's think step by step.' (P1) to generate a rationale R; stage 2 feeds R with X and P1 plus an answer-extraction trigger P2 such as 'Therefore, among A through E, the answer is'. Instructions taken from or inspired by Brown et al. 2020, Ouyang et al. 2022, Zhang et al. 2023a and Ding et al. 2022.

parameters.summary_length_limit_experiment: instruction 'Please summarize the given conversation in no more than 25 words.'
parameters.ner_split_instruction_experiment: GPT-3.5 instructed to generate each entity type separately

other.prompt_selection: for public models, results are reported for the best prompt found; for non-public models (e.g. PaLM) the best result in the corresponding paper is reported (Limitations)
other.reasoning_reporting: for each reasoning dataset the better of zero-shot and zero-shot-CoT is shown in Fig 1 and Table 11

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: exact-match accuracy on reasoning, NLI, QA, dialogue and sentiment datasets

metrics.name: ROUGE-1/2/L
metrics.definition: ROUGE scores on SAMSum (Fig 1 and Table 11 use the average of the three)

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: entity-level F1 on CoNLL03, overall and per class (Loc, Per, Org, Misc)

baselines: text-davinci-002, UL2-20B, LaMDA-137B, Codex, PaLM-540B (reported few-shot, Wei et al. 2022)
fine-tuned models per task: PaLM, CompassMTL, T5-11B, DeBERTa, BART, CODA, Flair, LUKE, ACE, MDFN, BiDeN, BERT, RoBERTa, GPT-2-FT and others
eval.protocol: Single run per dataset, no significance tests or confidence intervals. Baseline numbers are copied from earlier papers rather than rerun. In Table 11 the 'Fine-tuning' row is the best previous full-set or few-shot fine-tuning result among those in the paper, and for reasoning it is the few-shot result from Wei et al. 2022.

availability.data: Public benchmark datasets; the model is a closed API (OpenAI)

results.claim: With zero-shot CoT ChatGPT reaches 78.9% on GSM8K versus 59.5% for text-davinci-003.
results.table: Table 2, row ChatGPT, GSM8K CoT (text-davinci-003 CoT 59.5)

results.claim: ChatGPT scores 85.9% zero-shot on RTE, above GPT-3.5 (80.1), FLAN (84.1), T0 (80.8) and PaLM (72.9), but below the fine-tuned PaLM (95.8).
results.setup: RTE, zero-shot; FLAN, T0, PaLM numbers are reported from other work

results.claim: ChatGPT scores 89.3% zero-shot on CB versus 83.9 for GPT-3.5.
results.note: Only 56 test samples, so one example is about 1.8 points.

results.claim: On RTE ChatGPT is much better on the Entailment class (92.5 vs 70.6) but worse on Not Entailment (78.6 vs 90.8).
ChatGPT scores 87.3% on BoolQ, 2.6 points over GPT-3.5 but below PaLM (88.0) and fine-tuned T5-11B (91.2).
ChatGPT scores 76.2% on MuTual, 1 point above GPT-3.5 (75.2), below fine-tuned BiDeN (93.5).
ChatGPT's SAMSum ROUGE-1 is lower than GPT-3.5's (42.4 vs 44.0) and far below fine-tuned CODA (50.1).
ChatGPT's summaries average 36.6 words versus 23.3 for GPT-3.5 and 20.0 for ground truth, offered as the reason for lower ROUGE.
results.setup: SAMSum, default instruction without length control
results.note: Ground truth average is 20.0. A hypothesis, not tested by intervention on the cause.

results.claim: Adding a 25-word limit to the instruction cut ChatGPT's mean length to 22.8 words but lowered average ROUGE-1/2/L from 31.0 to 30.6.
results.setup: SAMSum, ChatGPT, instruction 'no more than 25 words'
results.quote: drops from 31.0 to 30.6. So we conclude that
results.note: A 0.4-point drop with a single run and no variance estimate.

results.claim: ChatGPT's overall CoNLL03 F1 is 53.2, similar to GPT-3.5 (53.5) and far below fine-tuned ACE (94.6).
Neither model can identify the Miscellaneous class (F1 4.1 for ChatGPT, 4.8 for GPT-3.5).
results.note: Authors suggest annotation-scope mismatch and label noise as partial causes.

results.claim: A prompt asking GPT-3.5 to generate each entity type separately drops NER F1 to 34.8.
results.quote: leading to a much lower F1 score (34.8).

results.claim: ChatGPT scores 93.7% on SST2, 4.9 points over GPT-3.5 (88.8), gains concentrated on negative samples (96.7 vs 89.5), below fine-tuned T5-11B (97.5).
Without CoT ChatGPT fails Last Letter Concatenation (0.4%) and does worse than text-davinci-003 on Coin Flip (21.8 vs 49.0); with CoT on Coin Flip ChatGPT (65.8) is far below text-davinci-003 (97.8).

results.note: Table 3 ChatGPT Coin Flip N/A is 21.8, Last Letter N/A is 0.4.

results.claim: On CSQA zero-shot, ChatGPT (73.7) is slightly below text-davinci-003 (74.9), and CoT does not help either model.
results.table: Table 3, row ChatGPT, CSQA N/A (text-davinci-003 N/A 74.9; CoT 71.5 vs 70.0)

results.claim: Across most tasks ChatGPT underperforms the best prior full-set or few-shot fine-tuned method (e.g. RTE 85.9 vs 95.8, CB 89.3 vs 100.0), so it is not a perfect generalist.
results.setup: Table 11, RTE, ChatGPT zero-shot vs fine-tuned PaLM
results.table: Table 11, row ChatGPT vs Fine-tuning, column RTE
results.note: Table 11 'Fine-tuning' row for reasoning datasets is the few-shot result from Wei et al. 2022; ChatGPT beats it on GSM8K (78.9 vs 63.1) and AQUA-RAT (53.5 vs 45.3).

limits: Authors concede cost limited the study to modest dataset sizes and 7 categories (Limitations).

Baseline results for non-public models are the best from the original papers, and for public models the best prompt found, so prompts are tuned for baselines but only a small set of prompt templates was explored for ChatGPT.
Zero-shot only: ChatGPT's few-shot in-context learning is not compared (stated in Limitations).
No decoding settings, number of runs, seeds or variance are given, so differences of a point or two (MuTual 76.2 vs 75.2, SAMSum length-limit 31.0 vs 30.6) are not shown to be significant.
Comparisons mix numbers the authors ran with numbers copied from other papers under possibly different prompts and splits.
Explanations (RLHF causing verbosity, preference for factual input, differing training data) are hypotheses with no ablation.
Closed API snapshot queried 06/15/2023 to 06/21/2023; ChatGPT has since changed, so absolute numbers have dated.
Several answers are not strict-format (e.g. 'It is unclear', 'neutral', 'mixed', refusals), and the paper does not say how such outputs were scored.
Does not check data contamination of the benchmarks.
